prize_parts.citation: for developing the political-economy theory of trade policy, showing how lobbying and special-interest politics shape the structure of trade protection

statement.case_for: My ballot and laureates are unchanged: B001, a single part crediting Helpman and Grossman. The citation is narrower than in round 1. The protection-for-sale model and the joint book on interest groups and trade policy turned a long-standing question, why trade policy departs from efficiency, into an equilibrium model of lobbying and government objectives. The model made sharp cross-sector predictions, and that is what let a large empirical literature test, qualify and sometimes contradict it. A framework that can be shown wrong in places is doing what a prize-worthy theory should. Credit is the cleanest on the shortlist: a long, tightly coupled two-person partnership with no co-originator at the same level left out. The core work is about three decades old and has been through extension, testing and textbook absorption. As a trade and industrial-organisation economist, I find that the framework changed how the field models policy formation, not just tariffs. I draw this assessment from the written round-1 arguments and my own reading. I do not treat the number of members who prefer B001 as evidence of merit, and I tested the case against the strongest alternatives below.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still empirical. Structural estimates of the protection-for-sale equilibrium are sensitive to specification and setting, and support for its predictions is mixed. The contribution is therefore more a disciplined framework and research agenda than a settled quantitative result. If the committee wants an award for tested findings, the design-based evidence in B018 or the validated estimation toolkit in B002 has an advantage. A second concern is distinctness from the 2008 trade prize and from any recent recognition of innovation-led growth. Both are reported in colleagues' files, and I have not verified them. A third is that Helpman is credited on B030 too. The committee should therefore treat the two trade ballots as alternative framings of a trade prize, not as additive parts. Finally, a citation confined to political economy is narrower than the pair's full body of work, and some members may regard that as understating it.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B002 for Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn on breadth of use and decades of practical validation. He calls B001 a close alternative, finds the mixed protection-for-sale record more worrying than B001 supporters do, and warns against widening the B001 citation to endogenous growth because that goes beyond the ballot's stated discovery.
responses.response: His warning on citation scope is the main reason my citation changed. In round 1 I included the innovation, growth and trade strand. His argument, and Fredriksson's and Enflo's, persuaded me that this stretches the discovery beyond what the ballot defines and invites the overlap question. The citation now rests on political economy alone. On the empirical record, I do not think the comparison with B002 is as one-sided as it looks. Structural IO estimates are also sensitive to specification and instruments. The difference is that BLP has been used in practice, in merger review, for three decades, while protection-for-sale is mostly an academic organising framework. I weigh that difference but do not treat it as decisive. B002 is my second alternative, and I disclose that it is my own field. If the committee wants a methods prize, I would support the BLP triple. Bresnahan and Reiss are a real cost of the three-name cap, as Krusell acknowledges, and I have not resolved that cost.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers B018 for Autor, Dorn and Hanson. She changed from Katz to Dorn to get a cleaner attribution and now words the citation around technology and trade shocks to labour demand. She treats a decade of replication and challenge as maturity, not a flaw.
responses.response: Her change from Katz to Dorn resolves my main attribution concern from round 1. I had objected that Katz would be a fourth name beyond a three-name cap. Autor, Dorn and Hanson is a stable set for the trade-shock evidence, and a citation confined to that evidence is defensible. I accept her argument that open debate on shift-share design and persistence can be read as maturity. I still weigh the same issues differently from her. The task-framework antecedents (Levy and Murnane, Acemoglu among them) are outside the credited names. The long-run magnitude of the effects is still being revised. A framework whose core has been absorbed for three decades seems to me more settled than a literature still being re-estimated. I keep B018 as my first alternative and could see it rising in a later year. This is a difference of weighting, not of view on quality.

responses.point: Dreber prefers B030 for Melitz and Helpman because the firm-heterogeneity framework has been tested densely against micro data. She names the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as its main weakness, and in round 1 she answered my ranking of B030 by saying selection changes the welfare accounting of trade and that Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple broadens the base beyond one paper.
responses.response: I accept her correction. Selection into exporting does more than refine older models. It changes how gains from trade are computed and which data researchers use, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exports versus foreign direct investment broadens the contribution beyond one paper. That is a stronger case than my round-1 description of a single pivotal paper conveyed. It does not remove my main reservation. The exporter facts and parallel models came earlier and independently from people not credited, and the three-name cap cannot fix that without weakening the Melitz-Helpman core. B001 has no comparable gap. Her point that denser empirical confrontation should count is fair, and it is the best argument for B030 over B001. I disagree about the empirical comparison. The part of B030 that is tested most densely is partly the exporter facts, which predate the theory and came from the people left out. I still treat B030 as a serious alternative, and as a different contribution by Helpman, not an additive one.

responses.point: Boppart prefers B003 for Obstfeld and Rogoff. He rests the case on the intertemporal framework and the Redux synthesis, with the puzzles as the living part. He grants that the puzzles have several originators and that Redux price-setting is not what current models rely on empirically.
responses.response: His separation of the durable framework from the vulnerable specification is the strongest form of the B003 case, and it moved me toward taking B003 more seriously. My work on exchange-rate pass-through and invoicing currency leaves me cautious about the exchange-rate puzzles as a basis for credit. Pricing and invoicing behaviour is part of why the disconnect is not resolved. Attribution there is spread across many contributors, and the puzzles are a shared agenda. If the citation rests on the framework alone, as he proposes, that concern is smaller. I still see B003 as having thinner attribution on its distinctive half than B001 has on its whole. I also find it harder to say how far the framework is a distinct discovery and how far it extends the Mundell-Fleming tradition. I ranked it fourth and keep it there, outside my two named alternatives.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee should give the mixed empirical record of protection-for-sale relative to its influence on theory and applied work. This is the main open scientific question.

Whether a citation confined to political economy is the right scope, or whether the committee would prefer to credit the innovation, growth and trade strand as well. That would need a clear argument that it does not rely on prizes already awarded.
Statements about the 2008 trade prize and the 2025 innovation-led growth prize come from colleagues' files. I have not independently verified them or checked how much they overlap with B001.
How to handle Helpman's credit on B001 and B030 if members divide between the two trade framings, and whether that division should affect the configuration.
Whether the B018 trio (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) can be cited as one discovery without claiming the task framework, and when persistence and identification evidence will be settled enough.
My assessments rest on my own general knowledge and colleagues' written statements. I have not independently verified citation or impact data.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Helpman or Grossman is apparent from my supplied profile. I co-authored with committee chair John Hassler, a B001 supporter, and with former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026). My profile lists co-authors Chad Syverson (Chicago Booth) and Itay Goldstein, among others. None is credited on B001, my alternatives B018 and B002, or B030. My fields are industrial organisation and international trade, so I may weigh B002, B030 and B001 more heavily than colleagues from other fields, and I have tried to apply the same criteria to every ballot. The public fact that I am married to a former Swedish prime minister is noted only for completeness, and I find no bearing on any shortlisted candidate. I disclose all of this without adjudicating it.
